book.entry: All entered symbols are opened at the first successful poll after SIM_START, at that poll's observed spot price (spot leg) and mark price (perp leg), with entry costs charged per the cost model. Declared difference from RD-009: the backtest entered at daily closes inside folds; a live paper book fills at observed prices at poll timestamps.
book.exit: Only via (a) a kill criterion below, (b) simulated liquidation, or (c) the coordinator ending the run. No discretionary exits, no threshold cells (RD-009 showed the F72-threshold POS cells were a 2024-H2 phenomenon; the forward question is the always-on book).
book.structure: always_pos only: long spot / short perp, coin-quantity hedge q fixed at entry, no rebalance trades (RD-009 mechanics verbatim). The NEG direction is excluded: RD-009 measured it NOT viable (expectancy -5.445%, PF 0.035, borrow-assumption-dependent).

universe.activation_rule: A symbol enters at sim start only if the start bundle carries a spot price, a mark price and a funding history for it. A symbol missing at start is recorded in SIM_START as NOT_ENTERED with the reason and is never added later (no survivorship repair mid-run).

clock.earliest_honest_evaluation: max(SIM_START + 6 calendar months, date of the 2nd confirmed regime turn). For a 2026-11-15 start the calendar bound is 2027-05-15; the turn bound can only push it later, and turn confirmation itself lags a flip by 14 days.
clock.proof_window_caveat: The delivery proof run spans hours, i.e. one to two funding settlements. Its PnL is NOISE by construction (expected funding over hours at the current regime is ~0.001-0.01% of notional against 0.19% entry costs already charged). The proof demonstrates accounting correctness and continuous operation, NOT performance.
clock.starts: At SIM_START (the timestamp of the first ENTRY rows).

costs.shadow_2x: Every PnL figure is ALSO tracked at 2x costs in parallel (fees and slippage doubled), so the RD-009 2x-cost check is evaluable at judgement without re-running anything.

endpoints_public_no_keys: GET https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/premiumIndex (mark prices, last funding rates, next funding times)
GET https://api.binance.com/api/v3/ticker/price (spot; the data-api.binance.vision mirror of the same API is an accepted substitute)
data_and_transport.gaps: A failed poll writes an ERROR row and the next successful poll backfills every missed funding print from fundingRate history (startTime-based). Marks are never backfilled or interpolated; a gap is a gap in the mark series and is visible as such.
data_and_transport.poll_cadence: Daemon default 300s. The sandbox proof run polls at ~900s because each poll is a bridge round-trip; funding prints are exact at any cadence (immutable history), only mark granularity coarsens, and that is declared wherever excursion figures from the proof window are quoted.
data_and_transport.sandbox_transport_disclosed: This sandbox's egress is geo-blocked by Binance (api.binance.com and fapi.binance.com return the restricted-location response; the futures websocket handshake times out). The sandbox PROOF RUN therefore fetches the IDENTICAL public endpoints via FRIDAY Server 1 (Hyderabad egress) through the bridge run_shell tool, in ONE batched server-side fetch per poll that returns a single JSON bundle filtered to the 30 declared symbols. The data is the same exchange data from the same endpoints; only the network vantage differs, and every MARK/FUNDING ledger row records transport='bridge-s1'. The server runbook (the durable deployment) uses direct REST from the server itself, transport='rest'.

evaluation_bar.fail_standard: Any required element missing at the judgement date is a FAIL or a NOT-YET-JUDGEABLE, stated as which. There is no partial promotion and no wiring anywhere on any outcome; a governed deployment proposal would additionally need the proven top-up/margin runbook and remains a separate owner decision (live trading gated).
pass_standard_all_required: Duration: >= 6 months elapsed since SIM_START AND >= 2 CONFIRMED funding-regime turns (definition below), whichever is LATER.

Forward net yield (1x costs, hypothetical close at judgement) >= the RD-009 W5 backtest rate of +1.29%/yr on one-leg notional, sustained over the window (annualised from the window's actual elapsed time).

Segment descriptive checks (the always_pos bar minus the episode count): pooled segment expectancy > 0; segment PF >= 1.2; breadth >= 50% of closed segments net positive; 2x-cost pooled expectancy > 0.
Zero unresolved kill trips: no BOOK STOP, no LIQUIDATION, and no SYMBOL DROP during the window (RD-009 section 7: 'zero kill trips'). A MARGIN_REVIEW is not a kill trip (declared above).
Accounting integrity: sanity identities T1 and T2 (below) pass on the full ledger at judgement.
evaluation_bar.unit_of_account_ADAPTATION: RD-009's episode (one symbol x one fold, force-exited at fold end) does not exist in an always-on forward book. DECLARED ADAPTATION: the unit is the SYMBOL-SEGMENT - a symbol's continuous holding from entry to exit (drop, kill, liquidation, or hypothetical close at the judgement date). The >=200-episode check and the Bonferroni machinery are declared INAPPLICABLE to at most 30 segments and are NOT smuggled in; in their place the RD-009 section 7 pass standard governs, exactly as RD-009 itself judged always_pos on labelled descriptive evidence rather than a bent bar.

funding.cashflow: For a print at time t with rate r: cashflow_i = -dir_perp * r * mark_at_print_i * q_i where dir_perp = -1 (short), i.e. the short RECEIVES q * mark * r when r > 0 and PAYS when r < 0. mark_at_print is the close of the 1-minute mark-price kline at the print timestamp (GET /fapi/v1/markPriceKlines), fetched with the print. If that kline is unavailable, the poll's current mark is used and the FUNDING row carries mark_approx=true (declared approximation, same spirit as RD-009's 1h-close approximation).
funding.source: ACTUAL settled prints from Binance USD-M GET /fapi/v1/fundingRate (public, no key), polled with startTime = last recorded print per symbol; prints are immutable exchange history, so poll cadence cannot distort them.
funding.window: A symbol earns exactly the prints with fundingTime in (entry_ts, exit_ts]. Prints already settled before entry are never credited.

kill_criteria: BOOK STOP (RD-009 section 7, verbatim): rolling-90d net PnL of the book after 1x costs < 0 -> the book is closed at that poll's prices, exit costs charged, the sim ends in state STOPPED_KILL and the forward verdict is FAIL-by-kill. (Cannot trigger before day 90 by construction.)

SYMBOL DROP (RD-009 section 7, verbatim): any held symbol whose funding flip (sum of its settled funding cashflows) costs > 5% of its one-leg notional within any rolling 30-day window -> that symbol is dropped: both legs closed at that poll's prices, exit costs charged, its segment closed, never re-entered. The sim continues with the remaining symbols; the drop is a KILL_TRIP for the pass standard.
LIQUIDATION: as defined in sizing_and_margin. Ends the sim; FAIL-by-liquidation.

ledger.form: Append-only JSONL. Every row carries: seq, ts_utc, type, prev_hash, row_hash (SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the row without row_hash), and for data-driven rows the bundle_sha256 of the raw poll bundle that produced them. Raw bundles are archived gzipped in the state directory. The ledger is the forward-measurement record: no row is ever edited or deleted; corrections would be new rows.

parent.governing_spec: RESULTS_RD9.md section 7 (Forward-test specification) is adopted as the governing spec for duration, logging, kill criteria and pass standard, with the adaptations declared below and nowhere else.

prohibitions: Paper only: no orders, no exchange accounts, no API keys, public GET endpoints only. No contact with the live Stratex daemon, the FWD forward lane, any production config, registry or server process. Research code in Stratex/rigorous_backtest/rd17/ only (the rd9/rd16 layout precedent).
question: Does the RD-009 always_pos funding-carry book (long spot / short Binance USDT-M perp, delta-neutral, coin-quantity hedge) harvest funding net of the RD-009 cost model when run FORWARD on live mainnet data, under a margin structure that RD-009's liquidation evidence says is survivable?

regime_turn_definition.counting: Confirmed turns are counted across held symbols (distinct symbol-events). The duration gate needs >= 2. The book-level pooled F14 sign (equal-weight mean across held symbols) is tracked descriptively alongside.
regime_turn_definition.daily_snapshot: At each 00:00 UTC snapshot (computed by the sim from its ledger at the first poll of each UTC day), for each held symbol: F14 = mean of its settled funding rates with timestamps in (snapshot - 14d, snapshot]. Symbols with no prints in the window carry their last F14 forward (prints are 8-hourly in practice, so this is a formality).
regime_turn_definition.source: RD-009 section 7: 'a held symbol flipping sign for >= 14 days', operationalised as follows.
regime_turn_definition.turn_event: A turn OPENS for a symbol on the first snapshot whose F14 sign differs from the F14 sign 14 snapshots earlier. The turn is CONFIRMED when the new sign persists for 14 consecutive daily snapshots; the confirmed turn is dated at its opening snapshot. A sign that flips back before confirmation is recorded as an UNCONFIRMED_FLIP (descriptive only).

sanity_checks: T1 (funding identity): an independent recomputation from the archived raw bundles reproduces the ledger's cumulative funding cash per symbol exactly (tolerance 1e-6 USDT). Run at delivery on the proof window and owed at judgement on the full window.

T2 (decomposition identity): for every symbol at every MARK, segment PnL == funding_component + basis_component - costs (tolerance 1e-6 relative), where basis uses current marks on both legs vs entry.

T3 (frozen-price unit test): on a synthetic bundle with frozen prices and zero costs, episode PnL equals the sum of funding cashflows exactly (the RD-009 S1 analogue), verified in the shipped test file.

sizing_and_margin.account_equity_definition: equity = sum_i spot_value_i + perp_margin_cash + sum_i perp_upnl_i + funding_cash - fees_paid_total, where perp_margin_cash starts at 1000 per entered symbol, funding_cash accumulates settled funding cashflows (signed), and perp_upnl_i = q_i * (mark_i - mark_entry_i) * (-1) for the short leg.
sizing_and_margin.liquidation_rule: If equity <= MM at any poll: SIMULATED LIQUIDATION event - the entire book is closed at that poll's prices, exit costs charged, the sim ends in state LIQUIDATED and the event is the headline of any report. (By construction this needs roughly a full-notional basis blowout; RD-009 measured era basis within +/-0.20% per symbol. It is armed anyway.)
sizing_and_margin.maintenance_margin: MM = sum_i (q_i * mark_i * MMR) with a flat declared MMR = 1.0% for every symbol (declared approximation of Binance's tiered maintenance-margin rates at this notional scale; conservative vs the 0.4-0.5% lowest tiers, below the highest alt tiers).
sizing_and_margin.margin_model: CROSS-MARGIN portfolio simulation (one account), chosen because RD-009's excursion census (intra-episode adverse perp moves: median +20.1%, p95 +109.5%, max +598%) proves a 3x ISOLATED perp leg would have been liquidated repeatedly. The perp leg is funded at 1.0x its notional in margin cash at entry (effective perp leverage 1.0x), and the spot leg's market value nets against perp losses inside the account equity, which is what cross margin means.
sizing_and_margin.topup_and_margin_review: ADAPTATION, declared: RD-009 section 7's excursion criterion (adverse excursion > 25% against the perp leg -> halt and reassess) was written for the 3x structure. In this 1.0x cross structure a 25% adverse move cannot threaten the account (the spot leg nets it; liquidation distance is ~100%+), so the 25% level instead logs a MARGIN_REVIEW event (per symbol and, in aggregate form, for the book when aggregate perp uPnL < -25% of initial perp margin cash). The event records the excursion, the account equity and the margin ratio at the time. The sim keeps marking after a MARGIN_REVIEW (paper measurement must not stop at the interesting part); a real deployment decision would reassess at that point. Max adverse excursion per symbol (vs its entry mark, from poll marks) is tracked continuously and reported.
sizing_and_margin.weights: Equal per symbol (q_i = 1000 / spot_entry_i). Results are reported in % of one-leg notional, so the paper unit size is scale-free.

status: Frozen before the simulation's first data point. The SHA-256 of this file is posted in the TASK-STR-RD-017 claim comment on issue #35 BEFORE the paper book is opened; the SIM_START ledger row repeats the hash. No ledger row, entry, or mark exists before that claim post.
title: Funding-carry forward PAPER SIMULATION on live mainnet data (the RD-009 forward test)
trial_accounting: This simulation is FORWARD MEASUREMENT, not a backtest. It adds ZERO trials to the programme's backtest trial floor (1,934 after RD-009; later rounds have raised it further - the floor is whatever the coordinator's current count says, and this task does not touch it). No parameter of this book was fitted on any data: structure, universe, costs and bar all descend from RD-009's frozen declaration and its section 7 spec.
